newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Walter sees 1995 profits fall.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Walter sees 1995 profits fall.

text.p: Germany's Walter Holding GmbH became another victim of the country's weak building markets on Friday as the company said its 1995 net profit fell to 102 million marks ($66.4 million) from 175 million before.

The Walter holding group, which comprises majority stakes in Frankfurt-listed Walter Bau AG, Heilit+Woerner Bau AG, Dyckerhoff & Widmann AG and Ed Zueblin AG, also said it was unable to be optimistic for the current year.
Walter said in a statement that 1996 results would be hit by the poor 1995/96 winter period, which restricted much of its domestic construction business.
Only in 1997, when it was planning rationalisation and restructuring measures, would profit improvements now be likely, it added.
The profit fall for 1995 came despite a slight increase in building output to 15.7 billion marks from 15.4 billion the year before.

German construction margins have suffered from price-cutting in slack domestic markets that are only expected to improve during 1997. Significant upturns in profits across the sector are not expected until 1998 at the earliest.
Hochtief AG, the country's second largest construction group, earlier on Friday said profits for the 1996 year were now expected to be below those of 1995.
